channel.title: Upshot: Essentials
channel.description: The week’s essential stories, with what to do about each.

item.title: Microsoft pushes emergency hotpatch to fix Windows Server crashes
item.description:
Microsoft released an emergency hotpatch fixing Windows Server 2025 crashes that followed installing the month's KB5131077 security hotpatch.

  • Microsoft released out-of-band update KB5138318 to fix Windows Server 2025 crashes after the November 2026 security hotpatch (KB5131077).
  • Affected servers with Router Advertisement enabled that receive time-bound IPv6 routes can stop with stop error 0x139 when a route timer expires.
  • KB5138318 downloads and installs automatically via Windows Update for hotpatch-enrolled devices, without requiring a restart.

What to do: If Windows Server 2025 crashes after KB5131077, install Microsoft's emergency hotpatch.

item.title: Exploited: Critical Juniper Session Smart Conductor Flaw Exploited in Attacks
item.description:
Critical flaw CVE-2026-103406 in Juniper Session Smart Conductor lets remote attackers run arbitrary commands as root, and it is being exploited.

  • Juniper and CISA warn that attackers are exploiting critical CVE-2026-103406 in Session Smart Conductor.
  • The flaw in the AutomatedProvisioner service could let remote attackers run commands as root via a crafted Salt minion ID.
  • Upgrade Session Smart Router and Session Smart Conductor to 7.2.3, 7.1.7, or 7.0.5, which include the fix.
  • CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog, urging federal agencies to patch within three days.

What to do: Patch now; root RCE is already exploited, so check exposed instances for compromise.

item.title: Exploited: Drupal Warns of New Highly Critical Site Takeover Vulnerability Under Active Exploitation
item.description:
Drupal warned of a highly critical Drupal core site takeover flaw, CVE-2026-136716, that is being exploited in the wild.

  • Drupal warns that CVE-2026-136716, a highly critical Drupal core site takeover flaw, is being exploited in the wild.
  • Sites that left install.php remotely accessible after the CVE-2026-132165 fix may have been compromised, including production sites.
  • Update to Drupal 11.4.14, 11.3.23, or 10.6.23; Drupal 11.0.x to 11.2.x and 10.5.x and below are end-of-life with no fix.
  • Check logs for unauthorized access, verify user 1's email is under your control, and consider resetting its password.

What to do: Patch Drupal core now; the site-takeover flaw is being exploited in the wild.

item.title: Exploited: Palo Alto Networks Patches Fragnesia Flaw Used to Root Firewalls
item.description:
A China-linked group chained PHP2Shell with the Fragnesia flaw in AI-assisted attacks on 25 servers; Palo Alto Networks has patched Fragnesia.

  • Palo Alto Networks released PAN-OS patches for Fragnesia, a Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw tracked as CVE-2026-46300 and used to root firewalls.
  • Attackers chained the flaw with PHP2Shell against PAN-OS firewalls with management interfaces exposed to the internet.
  • Apply the fixed PAN-OS versions in the advisory, and block direct web access to management interfaces, allowing only the management network or VPN.

What to do: Patch PAN-OS; also restrict management interfaces from internet, since chained attacks target them.
